finding.claim: Unauthenticated blind SSRF: POST /hooks/test passes attacker-controlled req.body.callback directly to axios.post with no scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation.

trace.note: Unauthenticated route handler on the pub router; no auth guard attached to pub.
req.body.callback used as the outbound URL without validation.
Upstream response status returned to the caller, giving a status-code oracle.

finding.guards_checked: No auth guard on pub (requireAdmin at routes.js:7-10 is attached only to admin, routes.js:12). No scheme allowlist, no host/IP allowlist, redirects followed by default in axios, method fixed to POST with fixed body {ping:true}. Mount point of pub not present in repo, so exposure unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:19-22 has no validation of req.body.callback, and no auth middleware is attached to pub. requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) is applied only to admin via admin.use at routes.js:12, and the candidate's note on that is accurate. The only other code in the repo is routes.js, so no other guard can be found.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (routes.js:19 pub.post, :20 axios.post with req.body.callback, :21 status returned), and nothing in routes.js:19-22 validates the URL, so if the pub router is reachable by unauthenticated clients the SSRF is real. The repo contains only routes.js and no app or mount file, so whether pub is reachable without auth (or sits behind an app-level guard) cannot be decided from the code available.

finding.claim: SSRF via admin diagnostics endpoint: GET /diagnostics/fetch fetches an arbitrary req.query.url server-side. Admin-only precondition; reported because it reaches internal networks and cloud metadata beyond what an app admin normally holds. Conditional, lower severity.

trace.note: Strict role check req.session.role !== 'admin' returns 403 otherwise.
req.query.url passed directly to axios.get with no validation.
Upstream status returned to the caller.

finding.guards_checked: Admin session guard present and correct (strict equality). No scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation. Status-only response. Mount point of admin not present in repo, so exposure unverified.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin at routes.js:7-10 (strict `req.session.role !== "admin"` returns 403) applied to all admin routes via admin.use at routes.js:12; no URL scheme, host, IP, or redirect validation exists before the sink at routes.js:15.
verdict.reason: The trace lines match the code (routes.js:8, 12, 15, 16), but the source req.query.url at routes.js:15 is reachable only by a session with role "admin" (routes.js:8, 12), so it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker, which the verification criteria require. The candidate's own claim concedes it is admin-only; the SSRF lacks the attacker-controlled source needed for a finding in this scope.
